The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee was appointed in January 1957 to review the CDP (1952) and the NES (1953); it reported in November 1957. October 1952 is the CDP launch and 1959 the start of Panchayati Raj.

The Committee sought constitutional recognition for PRIs and a Minister for Panchayati Raj in the State cabinet. Statement 3 is wrong: it wanted official participation of political parties at all levels of panchayat elections. So the answer is '1 and 2 only'.

West Bengal adopted the Ashok Mehta recommendations and strengthened its PRIs (Karnataka also followed). Rajasthan had pioneered the Balwant Rai Mehta three-tier model in 1959, and Tamil Nadu is cited only for a two-tier pattern.

Two tiers, a four-year term and party participation in panchayat elections are all Ashok Mehta recommendations. Option A belongs to L.M. Singhvi, option B to Balwant Rai Mehta and option D to G.V.K. Rao.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct: women are over 49.7% of elected panchayat representatives and 19 States/UTs reserve 50% of seats. Statement 3 is false: Article 243D(4) mandates at least one-third of seats and chairperson posts for women.
Under the Vikas Kishanrao Gawali triple test (2021), total SC+ST+OBC reservation must not exceed 50 per cent, so the 34 per cent BC quota plus SC/ST shares must stay within that 50 per cent ceiling.

K. Krishna Murthy (2010) upheld backward-class reservation in local bodies under Articles 243D(6) and 243T(6), holding that political backwardness is distinct from social and educational backwardness. It did not deal with tax distribution, SEC appointments or the term of Panchayats.
